parole.significato: A huge dog breed used in Argentina for big-game hunting which resembles a very large pitbull terrier.
parole.testo: From Spanish dogo argentino, from dogo (“molosser”) (from English dog) + argentino (“Argentine”).

parole.significato: A genre that emerged in late 1940s in Havana, influenced by the melodic and expressive style of vocal jazz.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish filin, itself from English feeling.
Borrowed from Spanish fútbol, from English football.

parole.significato: A final campaign rally done by candidates of one political party usually the night before an election.
parole.testo: From Spanish mitin de avance (literally “rally of progress; rally of advance”), from mitin + de + avance, where mitin itself is from English meeting. Compare Tagalog miting de abanse.
From Spanish narcodólar, from English narcodollar.

parole.significato: A racquet sport popular in Spain and Latin America, usually played in doubles on a small, closed court.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish pádel, from English paddle (tennis).
Borrowed from Spanish turista (literally “tourist”), from English tourist.

parole.significato: A citizen of the United States of America, as opposed to a Latin American.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Spanish yanqui, in turn from English Yankee, from Dutch (see more at said entry). Dated to 1914.
